data.cultural_impact: Dashratha is a revered and iconic name in Hindu mythology, particularly known from the epic Ramayana. As the name of the king who ruled Ayodhya, Dashratha embodies the power, authority, and righteousness of a king, as well as the importance of family and duty. His sacrifices for the greater good, including the exile of his beloved eldest son Rama, are profoundly remembered and respected.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper level, the name Dashratha can be seen as a reminder of the importance of self-sacrifice for the greater good. It can also represent the journey towards dharmic living, emphasizing the balance and harmony among the various aspects of life, depicted through the numbers ten - illustrating the ten chariots (representing the senses) and the ten avatars of Vishnu. Ultimately, the name inspires and encapsulates the virtues of love, duty, sacrifice, and the power and wisdom of a spiritual leader.

historical_references.reference: Dashratha was the king of Ayodhya, and the father of Rama, Sita and Lakshmana. He is most famously known for his unwavering devotion towards his wife Kausalya, who gave birth to Rama after a long wait and several trials.
Dashratha is also referred to as Dasaratha in various Hindu texts. He is said to have reigned in the Ikshvaku dynasty, which is believed to have originated around 1200 BC.
